chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who have faith.
But [He granted authority] over those who take him as their guardian and disobey His command.

key_terms.يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُمْ: Those who take him as guardian/ally

ai.seo_question: Who does Satan have authority over according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (a) clarification that Satan’s *sultan* (authority/power) is conditional, applying only to those who actively follow his whispers and neglect divine commands, rather than being absolute over all believers. This distinction underscores the Shia theological principle of human free will (*ikhtiyar*) and refutes the notion of predestined subjugation to evil, emphasizing that spiritual bondage is a result of conscious choice. The narration serves as a foundational proof for the possibility of *ma'sum* (infallible) individuals remaining free from Satan's influence while others remain susceptible.
